facts.statement: The ordinance amends the enforcement regulations of all four public medical insurance schemes — employees' health insurance, seamen's insurance, national health insurance and late-stage elderly medical care — for high-cost medical care limit-application certification, meal and life-care standard-copayment-reduction certification, specified-disease certification and eligibility confirmation certificate forms. It applies to insurers (health insurance societies, the Japan Health Insurance Association, municipalities, national health insurance associations, the seamen's insurance association and late-stage elderly medical care wide-area unions) and to insured persons and their dependants. It does not change who is insured and sets no benefit amount.

The ordinance itself adds no new duty for insured persons; it updates the references that existing duties point to. The amended regulations carry forward insurer and municipal certification duties: for example, National Health Insurance Enforcement Regulation Article 26-3 requires the municipality or association, when the conditions are met, to certify meal-cost reduction eligibility with a validity period. The certification duties are therefore obligations on insurers and municipalities, not new obligations created by this ordinance.

facts.statement: For the 2027-08-01 commencement, supplementary Article 2 of Ordinance No. 151 deems documents already in use under old forms to comply with the amended forms, and permits remaining old-form paper to be adapted and used for the time being. The only 2026-10-28 change is supplementary Article 3 (Form 13-2 reference, Article 103-2 to Article 103-7); it has no transitional provision of its own.

facts.statement: The amended regulations implement ordinance-level rules that the statutes delegate to MHLW ordinances: National Health Insurance Enforcement Regulation Article 26-3, for example, provides municipal or association certification of meal-cost reduction eligibility for a person specified by MHLW ordinance under Health Insurance Act Article 85(2), and this ordinance updates those rules to the renumbered enforcement-order items. The ordinance's own preamble and cited bases were read from the MHLW ordinance database PDF (browser read, not a fetched source); see unresolved.

facts.statement: MHLW presents the 2026 review as keeping the high-cost medical care system sustainable while protecting low-income and long-term patients: monthly caps rise and a new annual cap is introduced from 1 August 2026, the income bands are subdivided from 1 August 2027, and the multiple-occurrence amount for income below about 2 million yen is reduced by 25%. The review follows the expert committee's basic approach of 16 December 2025 and the Social Security Council Medical Insurance Subcommittee's deliberations. The consultation drew 2,758 comments and the draft was promulgated without change.

Insurers, municipalities, national health insurance associations and wide-area unions must update certification systems and forms to the 13-band references by 1 August 2027; insured persons face no change from this ordinance before then. From 1 August 2027 the applicable monthly cap follows the finer bands and the multiple-occurrence amount for income below about 2 million yen falls 25% (to 34,500 yen per the MHLW tables). Old-form documents are deemed compliant and old paper may be adapted and used for the time being.
